source.title: Cramming: Training a Language Model on a Single GPU in One Day

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied; minor PDF extraction artifacts, but relevant sections and tables are readable.
record.tranche_reason: Tests how architecture, optimizer, batch size, and dropout affect language-model performance in a new setting: masked-language pretraining under a one-day compute budget. It does not measure the natural-label versus random-label generalization gap directly.
record.gate_note: Rows capture the paper's own architecture, optimizer, batch-size, and dropout comparisons that bear on the claim's named conditions. Reported results about training throughput or MLM loss alone, and cited findings from prior work, are not rows.
record.test_reason: The optimizer ablations test V4 in a new language setting: masked-language pretraining under a one-day compute budget, evaluated by downstream MNLI accuracy. They do not isolate generalization from optimization or document a matched optimizer-tuning protocol. The batch-size experiments lack V5's fixed-epoch control, and the dropout experiments concern transformers rather than V6's fully connected or convolutional classifiers.
record.authors_conclusion: The record broadly captures the relevant statements, but the authors' overall conclusion is that a modified single-GPU, one-day pretraining pipeline approaches BERT on several GLUE tasks while scaling laws constrain gains from architecture changes. They retain decoupled-weight-decay Adam, find no advantage from alternative adaptive optimizers, use batch ramp-up for a small benefit, and disable pretraining dropout to maximize effective updates. Dropout is restored during downstream fine-tuning.
record.recipe_differences: One-day masked-language pretraining from scratch on text, with brief GLUE fine-tuning; optimizer and batch-size ablations evaluate downstream MNLI accuracy rather than train-test error gaps.
record.method_sensitivity: Batch-size performance depends on linear ramp-up and whether the target is pretraining loss or downstream MNLI. Dropout activation changes MNLI results. Optimizer results vary substantially between Adam/Adafactor and SGD in the reported setting.

fits_no_version.finding: Adafactor reaches 81.36/82.22 MNLI accuracy, close to the decoupled Adam recipes.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Different adaptive optimizers yield similar downstream performance in this compute-limited pretraining setup.

fits_no_version.finding: Batch-size and ramp-up choices affect pretraining and downstream optima under a one-day budget, with Figure 5 describing downstream differences as barely significant.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Optimal batch size under fixed wall-clock training can depend on whether the objective is pretraining loss or downstream accuracy.

fits_no_version.finding: Activating transformer pretraining dropout yields MNLI accuracy of 80.95/80.98, below the no-dropout recipes.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Disabling dropout during compute-limited, single-pass transformer pretraining can improve subsequent downstream accuracy.

record.problems: The paper studies a different objective and setting from the claim's core natural-label classification experiments. Optimizer comparisons are reported in one tabulated training variant; no uncertainty is stated. The batch-size result in Figure 5 is graphical, and its caption describes differences as barely significant without giving numeric values.
record.rows_left_out: No additional claim-bearing results beyond the extracted optimizer, batch-size, and dropout rows. Architecture experiments primarily report MLM loss, throughput, and downstream MNLI; they do not test convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers or width-dependent train-test gaps.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and the corresponding natural-label and random-label held-out accuracy comparisons.
Width beyond interpolation, zero training error, and test error after convergence.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity.

A documented matched learning-rate and schedule search; broader tuning; equal or better training performance accompanying worse held-out performance; switching from Adam to SGD; and word-level language-model evaluation.
Large- versus small-batch performance under equal epoch budgets, and recovery of that penalty through recipe changes.
Dropout in fully connected and convolutional classifiers, small-training-set effects, excessive-dropout underfitting, and joint removal with weight decay under augmentation.
Magnitude-aware sharpness, generalization gaps, and comparisons with norm- or margin-based measures.
Identification and removal of memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

missing.what: Classic-weight-decay Adam: MLM loss 7.44 and MNLI 32.28/32.39. Record alongside the decoupled-weight-decay recipe to capture V4's weight-decay clause.
missing.locator: Section 4.3, Choice of Optimizer; Appendix Table 10, Adam (classic WD formulation)

missing.what: RADAM: MLM loss 7.50 and MNLI 32.74/32.95, substantially below SGD's downstream accuracy.

Training losses for the optimizer comparisons: final clipped decoupled Adam 1.84, Adafactor 1.86, and SGD 7.46. These show that the downstream ordering is accompanied by major optimization differences.

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source for any listed version. Table 10 distinguishes the unclipped recipe from the final clipped recipe; the record conflates them. No uncertainty or matched optimizer-specific tuning search is reported for these comparisons.

versions.untested_parts: No fixed random-label training, natural-label comparison, or held-out generalization gap test.
No width sweep past interpolation with training and test error.
No convolutional versus fully connected comparison.

Tests Adam against other optimizers in a masked-language pretraining setting; does not compare held-out error with equal or better training performance on image or language benchmarks under the version's tuning protocol.
Varies batch sizes and schedules in a one-day pretraining setting; does not report a direct fixed-epoch large-batch versus small-batch comparison or compare language-model held-out performance.

Tests dropout in a language-model pretraining setting, reporting downstream MNLI performance; does not test the fully connected/convolutional classifier regimes or small training sets named in the version.
No sharpness, perturbation, or generalization-gap measurement.
No memorized-example identification, removal, or retraining test.

rows.subject: Adam
rows.operation_detail: Train with Adam using the final training variant; report downstream MNLI accuracy.
rows.note: No optimizer-matched baseline performance is supplied in the table row.
rows.check: The subject is a transformer trained with decoupled-weight-decay Adam, not an optimizer as a model. The reported 82.12/82.55 belongs to '+One Cycle, +Larger LR', before clipping. The final clipped recipe scores 81.79/82.14. Either adaptive baseline outperforms SGD's 59.30/58.02; identify which recipe the optimizer replacements use.

rows.subject: Adafactor
rows.operation_detail: Replace Adam with Adafactor in the final training variant; report downstream MNLI accuracy.
rows.note: Authors state that other first-order adaptive optimizers offered no advantages; Adafactor's displayed MNLI scores are slightly lower than Adam's.
rows.check: Adafactor versus decoupled-weight-decay Adam compares two adaptive optimizers, so this contrast does not test V4's adaptive-versus-SGD claim. The values 81.36/82.22 are correct, but 'partial' is not a state of the claimed effect. The asserted baseline also requires the clipping clarification in R1.

rows.subject: SGD
rows.operation_detail: Replace Adam with SGD in the final training variant; report downstream MNLI accuracy.
rows.note: This comparison uses a single stated setting; no broader tuning comparison is reported.
rows.check: The values 59.30/58.02 are correct. Describe the subject as a transformer pretrained with SGD. The final clipped adaptive recipe scores 81.79/82.14, whereas 82.12/82.55 is the preceding unclipped recipe. Optimizer-specific tuning and the exact replacement baseline are not documented.

rows.subject: Cramming BERT (A4000)
rows.operation_detail: Vary final batch size, with and without linear ramp-up, and report downstream MNLI accuracy.

conditions.value: figure sweep; individual values not stated

rows.note: The caption says differences are overall barely significant and notes a discrepancy between optimal pretraining batch size and optimal MNLI batch size with ramp-up.
rows.check: Figure 5 holds wall-clock time at one day, not epochs or processed examples fixed. Single-pass sampling does not establish equal data exposure across recipes. Its downstream MNLI sweep therefore cannot establish V5's fixed-epoch batch penalty. The caption's barely significant differences should not be treated as a clear effect.

rows.subject: Cramming BERT (A4000)
rows.operation_detail: Train with dropout activated instead of the final variant's disabled pretraining dropout; report downstream MNLI accuracy.
rows.note: The paper describes dropout as disabled during pretraining; this ablation activates it.
rows.check: This changes dropout during transformer MLM pretraining and measures downstream MNLI after fine-tuning; it does not test V6's specified classifier regimes. The dropout values 80.95/80.98 are correct, but 82.12/82.55 is the unclipped recipe; the final clipped recipe scores 81.79/82.14. Dropout is re-enabled during downstream fine-tuning.

relationships.condition: Decoupled-weight-decay Adam versus SGD under one-day transformer pretraining
relationships.reason: R1 and R3 show adaptive training reaching 81.79/82.14 with the final clipped recipe, versus SGD's 59.30/58.02. This qualifies an SGD advantage in this compute-limited setting; matched tuning and comparable training performance are not established.
relationships.display_finding: The adaptive recipe reportedly outperformed SGD, but the comparison remains unverified and matched tuning and training performance were unestablished.

relationships.condition: Classic Adam weight decay versus decoupled weight decay
relationships.reason: Table 10, missing from the rows, reports classic Adam at 32.28/32.39 versus decoupled Adam at 81.79/82.14 for the final clipped recipe, consistent with V4's weight-decay recovery clause; the large training-loss difference indicates optimization also changes.
relationships.display_finding: The reported improvement from decoupled Adam weight decay remains unverified, with training-loss differences also indicating optimization changes.

relationships.condition: Classic Adam and RADAM versus SGD in the reported training variants
relationships.reason: Table 10, partly missing from the rows, reports classic Adam at 32.28/32.39 and RADAM at 32.74/32.95, below SGD's 59.30/58.02 in R3; all have poor MLM loss, so this establishes a performance ordering rather than an isolated generalization gap.
relationships.display_finding: The reported lower performance for classic Adam and RADAM than SGD remains unverified and does not isolate a generalization gap.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Adam versus Adafactor in the final A4000 training setting
reader_labels.reason: The paper says other adaptive optimizers gave no advantage; Adafactor's MNLI scores are close to but below Adam's (R1, R2). This is not a direct held-out-error comparison matching V4's stated benchmark protocol.

reader_labels.label: challenges
reader_labels.condition: SGD versus Adam in the final A4000 training setting
reader_labels.reason: SGD's reported MNLI accuracy is much lower than Adam's in this setting (R1, R3), contrary to a general expectation that SGD should outperform adaptive methods; tuning scope is limited in the paper.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: A4000 batch-size sweep with linear ramp-up
reader_labels.reason: The batch-size figure reports that downstream MNLI differences are overall barely significant and the best batch size depends on the metric (R4).

reader_labels.label: challenges
reader_labels.condition: Dropout activated in the A4000 final training setting
reader_labels.reason: Activating dropout yields lower MNLI accuracy than the no-dropout baseline (R5), so this setting does not support the claim that dropout lowers held-out error.
